name: Immersa Core – Starter Templates, Elementor & AI Content
author: codefreex

sections.description:
Immersa Core is the free starter-site companion for the Immersa Builder theme.

Choose a starter site, follow the guided wizard, import the site, then customise it with Elementor or the block editor.

Watch our quick tutorial video below to see how it works.

Install Immersa Builder | Browse Starter Sites | View Pro Plans | Documentation

Launch a complete website faster

Immersa Core brings the essential website-launch workflow into one WordPress dashboard:

  • Guided website setup wizard
  • Bundled starter sites that work locally
  • Complete page, menu, widget and settings imports
  • Elementor-ready imports when included in the starter package
  • Gutenberg block patterns
  • Coming soon landing-page pattern
  • Global colour and typography presets
  • Required-plugin checks and administrator-controlled installation
  • Optional AI writing tools with no personal API key required
  • Optional premium starter sites and agency workflows through Immersa Pro

How it works

  1. Install and activate Immersa Builder and Immersa Core.
  2. Open the guided setup wizard.
  3. Choose a business type and starter site.
  4. Select your colours, typography and layout direction.
  5. Review required plugins before installation or activation.
  6. Import the starter site.
  7. Replace the demonstration content with your brand, images and offers.
  8. Edit supported pages with Elementor or Gutenberg.
  9. Optionally enable Themefreex Services for remote templates and AI tools.

Use a fresh site or staging environment and back up before importing.

Starter sites

Bundled starter sites are designed for Immersa Builder and can be imported without enabling a remote service. Included workflows provide starting points for agencies, coaches and local businesses.

A starter package can include:

  • Homepage and supporting pages
  • Navigation menus
  • Widget settings
  • Theme and global style settings
  • Gutenberg content
  • Elementor data when supplied by the package
  • Required-plugin information

Additional templates may be available through the optional remote catalog.

Elementor-ready templates

When Elementor is active and the selected package contains Elementor data, Immersa Core can import supported Elementor pages, builder metadata, full-width page settings and compatible templates so the pages are ready for visual editing.

Elementor can be installed or activated from WordPress.org only after administrator approval. Gutenberg layouts are not automatically converted to Elementor.

Gutenberg patterns and coming soon layouts

Immersa Core registers coming soon, hero and feature patterns that remain editable as normal WordPress blocks.

It does not automatically replace your homepage.

Optional AI content tools

After an administrator enables Themefreex Services, available AI workflows can help generate:

  • Blog starter drafts
  • Title and introduction ideas
  • Calls to action
  • Excerpts
  • SEO-friendly slug ideas
  • FAQs
  • Short page copy

No personal OpenAI API key is required. Generations use the Themefreex-managed credit balance shown in the dashboard.

Review AI output for accuracy, originality and suitability before publishing.

Immersa Pro

Immersa Pro is a separate commercial add-on. Immersa Core does not install or update Pro code.

Depending on the plan, Pro can add premium starter sites, higher AI limits, more activations, priority support, agency workflows and eligible white-label controls.

Compare current Immersa Pro plans

Import safety

Starter imports can create pages and apply menus, widgets and supported settings. Immersa Core uses allowlisted setting writes, but it is not a backup tool.

Before importing:

  • Back up the files and database.
  • Prefer a fresh site or staging environment.
  • Activate Immersa Builder.
  • Review required plugins.
  • Keep the browser open until import completes.
  • Check pages, menus, forms, widgets and mobile layouts afterward.
  • Replace all demonstration contact details and content before launch.

External services and privacy

Local templates and patterns work without Themefreex. Connected services require administrator consent.

When enabled, Immersa Core may send the following data to https://themefreex.com:

  • Service connection: site URL, site name, admin email, generated site token, WordPress version and plugin version.
  • AI generation: prompt, generation type, optional context, post ID, tone, word count, site URL, site token, timestamp, versions and HMAC signature.
  • Credit sync: site URL and site token.
  • Remote template import: selected template slug, site URL and licence key only for Pro templates.
  • Pro validation: licence key and site URL when Immersa Pro requests a licensed feature.
  • Help tutorials: request to the Themefreex tutorial endpoint.

AI prompts may be forwarded to Themefreex’s configured AI provider. Generated content and local history are stored on the WordPress site.

Tutorial thumbnails may load from https://img.youtube.com; Google or YouTube may receive the video ID, IP address, user agent and standard browser request data.

sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for Immersa Core.
  3. Install and activate the plugin.
  4. Install and activate the Immersa Builder theme.
  5. Open Immersa Core and start the setup wizard or starter-site library.
  6. Choose a starter site and review required plugins.
  7. Back up an existing website before importing.
  8. Import, customise and test the website before launch.

Enable connected templates or AI tools from Immersa Core > Core Settings > Themefreex Services after reviewing the disclosure.
sections.faq:
Is Immersa Core a theme?

No. Immersa Builder is the theme. Immersa Core is its companion plugin for starter sites, guided setup, imports, patterns and optional AI tools.

Do I need Immersa Builder?

Yes for the intended starter-site import result.

Are starter sites free?

Bundled local starter sites are free. More templates may be available through the optional remote catalog.

Does activation contact Themefreex?

No. Themefreex Services remain disabled until an administrator explicitly enables them.

Can I import into an existing website?

Yes, but back up first because existing content and settings can affect the result.

Does it work with Elementor?

Yes, when Elementor is active and the selected starter package contains Elementor data. The wizard can install Elementor from WordPress.org after administrator approval.

Does it work with Gutenberg?

Yes. Immersa Core imports supported block content and registers reusable patterns for the WordPress block editor.

Does it install plugins automatically?

No. It can offer to install or activate required WordPress.org plugins such as Elementor or Contact Form 7 only after an administrator starts the action.

Do I need an OpenAI API key?

No. Optional AI requests use Themefreex Services and the site’s managed credit balance.

What data leaves my website?

Only connected-service data described in the External Services section is sent after administrator consent. Bundled templates and local patterns do not require that connection.

Does Immersa Core install Pro?

No. Immersa Pro must be purchased, downloaded and installed separately.

Why did an import fail?

Check PHP memory, timeouts, permissions, required plugins, security rules and remote-request access, then retry on staging.

Where is the documentation?

https://themefreex.com/immersa-builder/docs/
sections.changelog:
1.0.12

  • Added early AI AJAX dispatchers so AI generation, credit refresh, history, and floating assistant requests are registered before WordPress handles admin-ajax.php.
  • Added logged-out AJAX responses for expired admin sessions so AI requests return a clear JSON error instead of WordPress’s bare 400 response.

1.0.11

  • Fixed AI Tools page bootstrap so the singleton is assigned before AI components initialize, preventing recursive initialization and 500 errors.
  • Restored floating Immersa AI assistant availability across admin pages after ThemeFreex Services are enabled.
  • Improved generation credit sync so local balances are updated from successful generation responses even if the follow-up remote balance refresh is unavailable.

1.0.10

  • Fixed AI component initialization so AI generation, credit refresh, history actions, and the floating admin assistant register on every admin and admin-ajax request.
  • Made the floating Immersa AI assistant available across Core admin pages after ThemeFreex Services are enabled, not only after visiting AI Tools.

1.0.9

  • Added the ThemeFreex-hosted services consent checkbox to the first setup-wizard step.
  • Defaulted first-step service consent to selected so remote starter sites, AI tools, credit sync, and license validation are enabled before the setup flow continues.

1.0.8

  • Allowed SVG media assets inside validated starter-site packages so demos with bundled SVG design files can import.
  • Seeded the free monthly AI balance locally before the first remote sync and retried credit refresh after automatic site registration.
  • Improved AI Tools styling fallback so the page does not render as an unstyled form if WordPress misses the normal enqueue hook.
  • Improved the floating AI assistant asset fallback so the chat widget can render reliably across admin pages after services are enabled.
  • Normalized Pro AI plan keys so the dashboard and AI Tools show the same paid-plan credit limits.

1.0.7

  • Fixed AI Tools loading when an AI dependency is missing or a prior AI class load leaves component classes unavailable.
  • Added direct ThemeFreex Services consent on the AI Tools page.
  • Added one-click install/activate actions for recommended WordPress.org plugins.
  • Marked Elementor and Contact Form 7 as required before starter imports, removed WPForms, and added Yoast SEO and PageForge as optional recommendations.
  • Added a dashboard promotion area for PageForge, RescueFill, and Nimora AI SEO.
  • Avoided the Core/theme constant collision that could raise an IMMERSA_CORE_PLUGIN_URL warning with the Immersa Builder theme active.

1.0.6

  • Added AI site-token recovery for upgraded installs where activation hooks did not create the token.
  • Kept AI credit refresh usable for valid AI users and returned the last local balance if remote credit sync temporarily fails.

1.0.5

  • Refreshed the WordPress.org plugin icon assets for the public listing.

1.0.4

  • Aligned the text domain with the WordPress.org slug for translation compatibility.
  • Kept starter-site importer writes constrained to allowlisted WordPress, widget, and Elementor settings.
  • Renamed the bundled WXR parser class to use the Immersa Core prefix.

1.0.3

  • Added the Immersa Core public identity.
  • Added reusable block patterns, including a coming soon landing page pattern.
  • Added optional AI tools behind explicit Themefreex service consent.
  • Kept bundled starter templates available locally by default.
  • Improved Elementor-ready starter package import support.

1.0.2

  • Improved starter template import compatibility and remote package handling.

1.0.1

  • Improved AI content tools for use from a companion plugin.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with setup wizard, starter templates, demo import, global styles, and admin dashboard.
